design:
**The approved mock is the design.** `hub/ui/src/components/panel/RunningTab.tsx` (presentational), its pure rules in `runningModel.ts` (which group an item falls in, what its row says, the filters, de-duplication), and `hub/ui/src/styles/running-panel.css`, all written for the mock and approved by the operator as rendered on 2026-11-12 (`hub/ui/mock`, route `#conversation/Architect/conv-9cdda4865e0b/running`; `hub/ui/mock/README.md`). Building this slice is wiring those components to the Hub's data, not redrawing them. Change the look only where the operator asks.

**Name.** Running, not Activity: the project already has an Activity tab (events, ledger, logs, traces).

**What the data has today (read 2026-11-12, for the builder's grounding).** Loops come from `useLoops` (`LoopSummary`: queue counts, current tasks with agent and capacity, `open_questions`, `stall_reason`, `firing_active`, ending state). Jobs from `useJobs` (`Job`, with `loop` set when the job is a loop's, `history` holding an `in_progress` run while it fires, `next_run`). Builds are read only per document (`SpecDocument.builds`, from the document's own read); the documents list carries each document's running build as done/total (`useBuildProgress`). No route lists builds across documents, so finished builds, and builds driven by a lead or by hand (which have no loop), are not available to a project-wide view without a Hub change. How to supply them is the builder's call; FR-2 states what must be listed.

**Where Answer goes.** A loop counts its open questions but the panel does not know which question. Answer takes the operator to where the question can be answered (the asking agent's conversation, with the question shown); if the Hub's loop record cannot name the question, it names the agent and conversation, and that is part of the Hub change this slice may need.

**Replacing Loops.** The `loops` index tab id is persisted per project in the browser (capability conversation-side-panel FR-6, FR-7). A Loops tab the operator had open reopens as Running; the loop detail tab (`LoopTab`) stays as the place a loop row opens, since only the index was judged bad.

problem: The panel's Loops tab (`LoopsIndexTab`) lists loops with one status badge and a count line. The operator, 2026-11-12: "it doesn't tell me anything, it's ugly and does not match the UI overhaul". It answers "what state is each loop in" rather than "what is happening now, and does anything need me", and it shows only part of the unattended work: spec builds and plain scheduled jobs are not in it at all, although since the overhaul most unattended work runs as builds.

requirements.rationale: The operator replaced Loops rather than adding beside it; a stale stored tab must not resurrect the old view or vanish silently.
requirements.statement: The side panel SHALL offer a Running index tab wherever it offered Loops (tab strip, plus menu, empty-state launcher with a count of items that need the operator or are working), and MUST NOT offer Loops any more. A Loops tab persisted from before SHALL be restored as Running, in the same strip position and visibility.

requirements.rationale: A build runs as a loop, and a loop is a job; showing all three layers would triple-count one piece of work.
requirements.statement: Running SHALL list every build of every specification document in the project (whatever drives it, running or ended), every loop that is not a build's, and every scheduled job that is not a loop's, and MUST list each piece of work exactly once.
Running SHALL group items in this order, leaving empty groups out: Needs you, Working now, Between steps, Scheduled, Paused, Finished, Stopped early; each group heading SHALL show its item count.

requirements.rationale: The operator's complaint was that the old tab did not say what needs them.
requirements.statement: An item that has not ended SHALL be in Needs you when its work has an unanswered question or when the Hub would refuse its next firing. Its row SHALL say which, in one sentence (the stall reason as the Hub states it), and offer Answer for a question or Look for a refused firing. Answer SHALL take the operator to where that question can be answered, and Look to the item's own record.

Each row SHALL show the item's name, its kind (Build, Loop or Job), the one time that matters for its group in relative words (started, next, ended or last ran), tasks done out of total where the item has a queue, the amount spent where a build has spent any, and up to two agents each with what they are doing (building, checking, holding, next on, running) and on which task, followed by "and N more" when there are more; where nobody is working it, one status line instead (for a job, its schedule).

Running MUST NOT show raw ids, cron expressions or event names. A schedule the app cannot say in words SHALL read "On its own schedule", and an amount or time SHALL be formatted the way the rest of the app formats it.

Running SHALL offer a Now / Finished / All filter, defaulting to Now (everything that has not ended), with each choice's count shown, and a filter by kind (Everything, Builds, Loops, Jobs) that narrows the list and the counts together; a filter that leaves nothing SHALL say so rather than show an empty box. A summary line above the filters SHALL count items that need the operator, are working, and are waiting.
Selecting a row SHALL open the item: a build opens its specification document in the panel at its builds, a loop opens the loop's detail tab, and a job opens the Jobs page.

Running SHALL reflect a change in a build, loop, job or question (a task taken, a firing started or ended, a question asked or answered) without the operator reloading, as quickly as the panel's other live views do.
Running SHALL render as the mock approved on 2026-11-12 does, in dark and light, at the panel's narrowest width without horizontal scrolling.

in_scope: A Running index tab in the conversation side panel, replacing the Loops index tab everywhere it is offered (strip, plus menu, empty-state launcher)
Listing builds, loops and scheduled jobs together, each once, grouped and filtered as the approved mock shows
Supplying the data that needs: including builds of every document, running and ended
Opening an item from its row, and answering or looking at what needs the operator
Restoring a previously open Loops tab as Running
non_goals: Redesigning the loop detail tab (`LoopTab`) or the Jobs page
Starting, stopping, pausing or editing builds, loops or jobs from the Running tab
Answering a question inside the Running tab itself
The other roadmap slices: Changes, Files, Terminal, Watch
Notifications or sounds for new needs-you items

summary: The conversation side panel's Loops tab is replaced by a Running tab: every build, loop and scheduled job in one list, grouped so that what waits on the operator comes first, each row saying what is happening now, with a Now / Finished / All filter and a filter by kind. Built from the mock the operator approved on 2026-11-12.
